title: State of Maharashtra v. Vijay Jadhav & Ors. (Shakti Mills Gang Rape)
crime_type: Abandoned Urban Mill Ambush / Repeat Gang Rape / Threat of Knife Violence
court_or_authority: High Court of Bombay / Sessions Court Greater Mumbai
legal_citation: 2021 SCC OnLine Bom 4220; Confirmation Case No. 1/2014
source: Bombay High Court Judgment & Indian Kanoon
ipc_sections: Section 376E IPC (Repeat rape offender provision introduced by Criminal Law Amendment Act 2013)
location: Shakti Mills Compound, Mahalaxmi, Mumbai, Maharashtra, India
evidence: Broken beer bottles and telephone belt cords used to bind the male colleague of photojournalist victim in mill ruins
DNA semen profiles matching the identical three suspects to a prior unsolved gang rape of a telephone operator at the same mill compound weeks earlier
Stolen camera memory cards and mobile phone recovered from suspect residential slums in Dhobi Ghat
Detailed forensic reconstruction of isolated, overgrown 16-acre dilapidated textile mill compound
modus_operandi: Lurked inside abandoned, overgrown textile mill ruins in central Mumbai. Confronted young photojournalist and her male colleague taking architectural photographs. Fabricated false allegations of trespassing, tied up the male companion with cords, dragged the woman into a ruined boiler room, and committed brutal gang rape while threatening them with broken beer bottles.
personality_disorder: Predatory territorial opportunism, pack-animal sexual violence, and persistent antisocial deviance.
common_traits: Exploiting abandoned urban industrial ruins and neglected public land
Falsely accusing trespassers to isolate and disarm them
Tying male companions with cords to immobilize resistance
Repeat predatory gang rape across consecutive weeks
summary: First landmark judicial test of Section 376E IPC (repeat rape offenders) enacted post-Nirbhaya. The Bombay High Court affirmed the heinousness of repeat offenders operating in urban ruins, commuting death sentences to rigorous imprisonment for the remainder of their natural life without parole.
